```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(psych)
library(knitr)

# ---- Load cleaned data (produced by 01_clean.R) ----
if (!file.exists("Data_A_clean.rds"))
  stop("Run 01_clean.R first to produce Data_A_clean.rds")
Data_A <- readRDS("Data_A_clean.rds")

# ---- Raw-state constants (from the audit, pre-cleaning) ----
n_raw      <- 199
n_raw_cols <- 40

# ---- Helper functions ----
fmt <- function(x, digits = 1) {
  if (length(x) == 0 || is.na(x)) return("—")
  formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
}

num_table <- function(df, vars, labels) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(vars), function(v) {
    x <- df[[v]]
    data.frame(
      Variable = labels[[v]],
      n        = sum(!is.na(x)),
      Missing  = sum(is.na(x)),
      Mean     = fmt(mean(x,   na.rm = TRUE)),
      SD       = fmt(sd(x,     na.rm = TRUE)),
      Median   = fmt(median(x, na.rm = TRUE), 0),
      Min      = fmt(min(x,    na.rm = TRUE), 0),
      Max      = fmt(max(x,    na.rm = TRUE), 0),
      check.names = FALSE
    )
  }))
}

# ---- Defensive check: recoded columns exist ----
required <- c("marital_clean","education_clean","disease_clean","regimen_clean",
              "condom_clean","alcohol_clean","smoking_clean","transport_clean",
              "sport_clean","art_start_year")
missing_cols <- setdiff(required, names(Data_A))
if (length(missing_cols) > 0)
  stop("Missing recoded columns: ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "),
       ". Re-run 01_clean.R.")
```

# Data cleaning and preparation

The raw dataset contained `r n_raw` records and `r n_raw_cols` variables, all initially stored as character strings. The following changes were made before analysis. The full cleaning code is in `Data_A_clean.R`; this section describes *what* was done.

## 1. Column name normalisation

Original Excel headers contained spaces and inconsistent capitalisation (e.g. `No. of sexual partners`, `no of H/H members`). These were standardised to snake_case using `janitor::clean_names()`.

## 2. Missing-value codes harmonised

The string codes `"no record"`, `"n/a"`, `"n.a"`, `"m/a"`, `"NA"`, and `"n/n"` were converted to `NA`. Character fields were trimmed and lowercased.

## 3. Numeric variables extracted from text

Several numeric variables were stored as descriptive text and were parsed:

- `age` — plain numeric years.
- `no_of_h_h_members` — e.g. `"4 H.H members"`.
- `no_of_sexual_partners` — spelled-out numbers (`"one"`, `"two"`) converted.
- `children_ever_born` — `"nil"`/`"none"` → 0; `"no record"`/`"unspecified"` → missing.
- `viral_load_level_on_initiation` / `viral_load_on_reincoportation` — e.g. `"120 copies of vl"` → 120 copies/mL.
- `cd4_vount_level` / `cd4_on_reincorporation` — cells/µL.

## 4. Date parsing and year of ART initiation

Values in `length_of_time_on_art` were **ART start dates written as text** (e.g. `"since 4 march 21"`), not durations. These were parsed to dates after correcting five month-name typos (`une`→June, `junly`/`julu`→July, `sug`→August, `ay`→May). Twelve records marked `"never been on art"` were assigned a missing start date.

Because the data-collection date was not recorded in the dataset, time on ART could **not** be computed. **Year of ART initiation** is reported instead.

## 5. Excel date serials in duration fields

Five records in `period_on_tb_treatment` and one in `length_of_time_on_art` contained 5-digit values (44,000–45,000) consistent with Excel date serials, not durations; these were set to missing. Records marked `"never been on isoniazid"` were coded as 0 months of TB treatment.

## 6. Categorical harmonisation

Typos and casing variants were collapsed:

- **Yes/no fields** — `"ye"`, `"Yees"` → yes; `"no."`, `"not …"` → no.
- **Educational level** — `"primary sch."`, `"primary scholling"` → primary.
- **Disease status** — `"HI"`, `"HV"` → HIV; `"Both HIV & TB"` → HIV & TB.
- **Regimen** — `"ARRT"`, `"art"` → ART; `"Both ART & TB treatment"` → ART & TB.
- **Condom use** — `"ye, condom use"`, `"yes, use condoms"` → yes.
- **Transport** — `"biycle"`, `"bycle"` → bicycle; `"no mention"`/`"unspecified"` → missing.
- **Marital status** — `"ma"` → married.

## 7. Variables excluded

`residential_area` was dropped: all `r n_raw` records were rural, so the variable has no variance. No duplicate rows were found.

## 8. Missing data

Missing values were **not imputed**. Two kinds of missingness are distinguished in the tables:

- **Data missingness** — information that should have been recorded but was not. For example, children ever born is missing for `r sum(is.na(Data_A$children_num))` records (`r round(mean(is.na(Data_A$children_num)) * 100)`%).
- **Structural missingness** — information that does not exist for certain patients. For example, LTFU period and re-incorporation VL/CD4 apply only to patients who were ever LTFU and returned.

# Results

## Numeric variables

```{r numeric-table}
num_vars <- list(
  age_num             = "Age (years)",
  hh_members_num      = "Household members (n)",
  sexual_partners_num = "Sexual partners (n)",
  children_num        = "Children ever born (n)",
  time_on_tb_tx_num   = "TB treatment duration (months)",
  ltfu_period_num     = "LTFU period (months)",
  vl_initiation_num   = "Viral load at ART initiation (copies/mL)",
  cd4_initiation_num  = "CD4 at ART initiation (cells/µL)",
  vl_reincorp_num     = "Viral load at re-incorporation (copies/mL)",
  cd4_reincorp_num    = "CD4 at re-incorporation (cells/µL)"
)

kable(num_table(Data_A, num_vars, num_vars),
      caption = "Table 1. Summary of numeric variables.",
      align = c("l","r","r","r","r","r","r","r"))
```

## Year of ART initiation

```{r year-table}
yr <- Data_A %>%
  filter(!is.na(art_start_year)) %>%
  count(art_start_year, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(`%` = sprintf("%.1f%%", n / sum(n) * 100)) %>%
  rename(Year = art_start_year)

kable(yr,
      caption = paste0("Table 2. Year of ART initiation (n = ",
                       sum(yr$n), ")."),
      align = c("l","r","r"))
```

## Categorical variables

```{r cat-tables, results='asis'}
cat_vars <- c(
  gender                        = "Gender",
  marital_clean                 = "Marital status",
  education_clean               = "Educational level",
  employment_status             = "Employment status",
  disease_clean                 = "Disease status",
  regimen_clean                 = "Regimen type",
  condom_clean                  = "Condom use",
  alcohol_clean                 = "Alcohol consumption",
  smoking_clean                 = "Smoking habit",
  transport_clean               = "Mode of transport to health facility",
  sport_clean                   = "Participation in sport",
  type_of_religion              = "Religion",
  distance_from_health_facility = "Distance from health facility"
)

for (v in names(cat_vars)) {
  x <- Data_A[[v]]
  t <- table(x, useNA = "ifany")
  df <- data.frame(
    Category = names(t),
    n        = as.integer(t),
    `%`      = sprintf("%.1f%%", as.integer(t) / sum(t) * 100),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  cat("\n\n**", cat_vars[[v]], "**\n\n", sep = "")
  print(kable(df, row.names = FALSE, align = c("l","r","r")))
  cat("\n")
}
```

# Notes on interpretation

- **Viral load units.** Viral load is reported in copies/mL as recorded in the source data. The median VL at ART initiation (`r fmt(median(Data_A$vl_initiation_num, na.rm = TRUE), 0)` copies/mL) is unusually low for a treatment-naive cohort and should be verified against the source data.
- **Structural missingness.** LTFU period and re-incorporation VL/CD4 have high missingness (`r sum(is.na(Data_A$ltfu_period_num))`, `r sum(is.na(Data_A$vl_reincorp_num))`, and `r sum(is.na(Data_A$cd4_reincorp_num))` records missing, respectively) because these variables are only applicable to the subset of patients who were LTFU and returned to care. These rates should not be interpreted as data-quality failures.
- **Children ever born.** Missing for `r sum(is.na(Data_A$children_num))` of `r nrow(Data_A)` records (`r round(mean(is.na(Data_A$children_num)) * 100)`%). Summary statistics are therefore computed on n = `r sum(!is.na(Data_A$children_num))`.
- **Time on ART** could not be computed because the data-collection date was not recorded; year of ART initiation is reported instead (Table 2).

```{r appendix-cleaning, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
# See 01_clean.R for the complete pipeline. Key steps:
# 1. janitor::clean_names()
# 2. NA-code harmonisation across character columns
# 3. parse_number() extraction for numeric-from-text columns
# 4. parse_since() date parser for length_of_time_on_art

saveRDS(Data_A, "Data_A_clean.rds")
```

# Logistic Regression: Predictors of LTFU

To identify independent predictors of LTFU, a multivariable logistic regression model was fitted.

```{r regression-table}
library(broom)
library(pROC)
library(ResourceSelection)

# 1. Recreate the outcome variable
Data_A <- Data_A %>%
  mutate(ltfu = case_when(
    ever_ltfu_clean == "yes" ~ 1,
    ever_ltfu_clean == "no"  ~ 0,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  ))

# 2. Fit the model
form_clean <- ltfu ~ gender + alcohol_clean + smoking_clean + 
                      hh_members_num + art_start_year
multi_clean <- glm(form_clean, data = Data_A, family = binomial)

# 3. Print the table (with publication-ready row names)
tidy(multi_clean, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(
    Predictor = case_when(
      term == "gendermale" ~ "Male gender",
      term == "alcohol_cleanyes" ~ "Alcohol consumption",
      term == "smoking_cleanyes" ~ "Smoking",
      term == "hh_members_num" ~ "Household members",
      term == "art_start_year" ~ "Year of ART initiation"
    ),
    OR = sprintf("%.2f", estimate),
    CI = sprintf("%.2f - %.2f", conf.low, conf.high),
    p  = ifelse(p.value < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p.value))
  ) %>%
  select(Predictor, OR, CI, p) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Adjusted Odds Ratios for Loss to Follow-Up")

# 4. Calculate metrics for the text below
auc_val <- round(as.numeric(pROC::auc(pROC::roc(multi_clean$y, multi_clean$fitted.values, quiet = TRUE))), 3)
hl_p    <- round(ResourceSelection::hoslem.test(multi_clean$y, multi_clean$fitted.values, g = 10)$p.value, 3)
```

**Model fit:** The model demonstrated acceptable discrimination (AUC = `r auc_val`) and good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow p = `r hl_p`).
